entities.name: Yuri Nemyrych
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Yuri Nemyrych (c. 1612 – 1659), also known as Jerzy Niemirycz, was a prominent Polish-Lithuanian magnate, Ruthenian nobleman, and a key political figure in the mid-17th century. Born into a wealthy Orthodox family that later converted to Arianism (Socinianism), Nemyrych received an extensive European education, studying at Leiden, Oxford, and Paris, which shaped his cosmopolitan worldview and intellectual prowess. He emerged as a leading advocate for a reconfigured Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, specifically championing the rights and autonomy of the Cossack Hetmanate and Ruthenian nobility, making him a pivotal, albeit ultimately tragic, figure in the tumultuous era of the Deluge and the Khmelnytsky Uprising.

Nemyrych's most significant contribution was his instrumental role in drafting and negotiating the Treaty of Hadiach in 1658. As a close advisor and chancellor to Cossack Hetman Ivan Vyhovsky, he envisioned the transformation of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth into a tripartite Polish-Lithuanian-Ruthenian Commonwealth, granting the Ruthenian lands (Ukraine) equal status and autonomy within the union. This bold proposal aimed to integrate the Cossack Hetmanate as the Grand Duchy of Ruthenia, with its own administration, army, and Orthodox metropolitan, while maintaining religious freedom for Arians like Nemyrych. He personally traveled to Warsaw to present and defend the treaty before the Sejm, securing its initial acceptance by the Polish diet.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Yuri Nemyrych's authorship of the Treaty of Hadiach (1658) offered a radical, albeit failed, vision for a tripartite Polish-Lithuanian-Ruthenian Commonwealth, directly impacting the political trajectory of Ukraine and the decline of the Polish-Lithuanian state.
